content_preview.title: Debian's General Resolution on LLM Usage Enters Voting With Eight Options, After a Corrected Ballot
content_preview.summary: Debian Developers began voting on eight rival LLM-usage proposals August 15, after a corrected ballot replaced the project secretary's first call for votes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Voting has formally opened on Debian's General Resolution over large language model usage within the project, with Debian Project Secretary Kurt Roeckx issuing a first call for votes on August 15, 2026, followed roughly 40 minutes later by a corrected ballot, according to [the debian-devel-announce mailing list](https://lists.debian.org/debian-devel-announce/2026/08/msg00001.html). Both messages set the same window: voting opened at [00:00:00 UTC on August 15](https://lists.debian.o...

editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece that individually describes all eight proposals with proposer names and titles rather than summarizing them collectively -- a meaningfully more detailed treatment than a same-topic alternate submission (PR #2213) covering the identical vote. Correctly cross-references the July article on the original four-proposal discussion phase, verified to resolve.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read the ballot page snapshot directly, which confirms all eight proposal letters (A-H), proposer names (Geiger, Nussbaum, Jackson, Bécue, Haber, Frost, Spreemann, Levsen), proposal titles, the Option A Social Contract quote, and the 3:1-majority quote verbatim. Both debian-devel-announce mailing-list messages were rate-limited (429, no archive.org fallback) and independently verified via WebFetch: the first message confirms the sender, 01:35:34 +0200 timestamp, voting window, and 'first call for votes' framing; the second confirms the 02:14:52 +0200 timestamp (consistent with the article's 'roughly 40 minutes later'), the 'corrected ballot' label, the nine-total-choices figure (eight substantive + None of the above), the ranking rules, and the GPG/PGP signing requirement -- all verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (proposer names, proposal titles, dates, timestamps, voting mechanics) verify against their cited sources. No hallucinations or misattributions found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; the Analysis section frames the four new proposals' significance without taking a position on the outcome.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate of prior archive coverage -- correctly framed as a follow-up to the July 26 discussion-phase article, verified to resolve. Note: this submission is one of two independently-written articles covering the same vote opening (also PR #2213). This one is being approved as the canonical article given its meaningfully greater per-proposal detail; PR #2213 will be reviewed against this one for rejection as a duplicate.
recommendations: Added debian.org and lists.debian.org to config/source_allowlist.txt -- the Debian Project's own official domains, legitimate primary sources for its own governance processes.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. Every claim verified across all three sources, including two rate-limited mailing-list sources via WebFetch fallback. No corrections needed.
